Q12418: Look at her smile: sometimes it seems to be there, sometimes it hides. Now look for her eyebrows — she has almost none!
Leonardo da Vinci blended his colours so softly, like smoke, with no hard lines. That is why her face seems alive and mysterious.
Q45585: Count the stars and find the yellow moon. Then spot the dark cypress tree — it looks like a green flame.
Vincent van Gogh painted it in the daytime, remembering the view from his window at the hospital where he was resting. He swirled the sky with thick strokes of paint.
Q185372: Find the tiny white dots of light on the pearl, in her eyes and on her lips. The pearl itself is just a couple of brushstrokes!
Nobody knows who the girl was; Johannes Vermeer may have painted an imagined face. The blue of her turban was made from a precious stone, lapis lazuli.
Q29530: Find the flag with three colours — red, white and blue. Far away in the smoke, look for the two towers of Notre-Dame.
The woman with the flag is not a real person: she is Liberty itself, painted as a brave heroine. Eugène Delacroix painted it about an uprising in Paris that same year.
Q219831: Among the men, find a girl in a golden dress who glows as if lit by a torch. Then look for the little dog at the bottom right.
It is actually daytime: old varnish turned dark, so people called it a night scene. Rembrandt showed the guards on the move, not standing neatly in a row.
Q151047: Find the winds on the left with puffed-out cheeks: they are blowing, and roses fly around them. What is Venus standing on? A giant seashell!
Sandro Botticelli painted an ancient myth: the goddess was born from sea foam, and the wind blew her ashore. He mixed his paints with egg yolk.
Q208758: Find the painter with his brush, the big sleepy dog, and the mirror on the back wall. Who can you see in the mirror?
The mirror shows the king and queen, so they must be standing where we are! Diego Velázquez made a puzzle picture: who is he really painting?
Q154469: Count the people around the table and find the steam rising from the potatoes. Look at their big, hard-working hands.
Vincent van Gogh wanted to show that these people eat with the same hands that dug the earth. He chose dark colours on purpose — the colour of a dusty potato.
Q328523: Find the orange sun and its path of light on the water. How many little boats can you see in the morning mist?
Claude Monet painted this harbour very quickly to catch a single moment. A critic made fun of the word 'impression' in the title, and that is how the Impressionists got their name.
Q698487: Compare the patterns: the man's robe has black and white rectangles, the woman's dress has circles and flowers. Find the flowery meadow at the bottom.
Gustav Klimt used real gold — thin gold leaf stuck onto the painting. His father was a gold engraver, so Klimt grew up loving its shine.
Q1752990: Look at Socrates' hand: he points a finger up, as if talking about something very important. Count his friends — who has turned away because they are sad?
Socrates was a wise man in Ancient Greece who taught people to ask questions. Even on his last, sad day he calmly kept teaching his friends.
Q474338: Find the white ermine in the lady's arms. Notice how the lady and the animal turn their heads the same way!
Leonardo da Vinci painted very few portraits of women, and this is one of the loveliest. The ermine was a sign of purity and goodness.
Q1892745: Find the clear crystal ball in Christ's hand. Then look at his hair: every curl twists like a little spring.
In 2017 it became the most expensive painting ever sold, for about 450 million dollars. Experts still argue about how much of it Leonardo da Vinci painted himself.
Q311243: We only see the wanderer from behind. Find the sharp rocks peeping out of the fog like little islands.
Caspar David Friedrich hid the man's face so that we can imagine standing in his place. He drew the mountains in sketches and put the picture together in his studio.
Q478271: Count how many laughing faces you can find! Look for the scribe with a quill pen — he is writing down their cheeky answer.
The Cossacks are writing a bold letter to the Turkish sultan and laughing at every joke. Ilya Repin worked on this painting for more than ten years.
Q464782: Find the pitchfork in the farmer's hand — its shape is repeated in the stitching on his overalls. Then find the pointed window at the top of the house.
The painting is named after that old 'Gothic' style window. Grant Wood's sister and his dentist posed for it, and they never posed together.
Q167605: Find the thin stream of milk pouring from the jug. Look at the bread: it is covered in tiny bright dots, as if it sparkles.
Johannes Vermeer turned an ordinary moment in a kitchen into something magical. Soft light comes from the window on the left, and dots of paint make the bread look crunchy.
Q683274: Find the bright spots of sunlight shining through the leaves onto dresses and the ground. How many dancing couples can you see?
Pierre-Auguste Renoir painted it on the spot, at an open-air dance in Paris, and his friends posed for it. He wanted to catch the happy mood and the dancing light.
Q220859: Find the round mirror on the back wall: it shows two more people at the door! Then look for the fluffy little dog at the couple's feet.
Above the mirror, Jan van Eyck wrote in Latin 'Jan van Eyck was here', like a signature. He used oil paints and showed every tiny detail.
Q2282256: Among the blue irises, find the one white flower. See how the long leaves bend and curve like swords.
Vincent van Gogh painted these flowers in the garden of the hospital where he was resting. He learned the bold outlines and bright colours from Japanese prints.
Q634122: Find the three paths running off in different directions. How many black crows are flying over the yellow field?
Vincent van Gogh wrote that fields under stormy skies could show both sadness and the strength of the countryside. He laid on thick, quick strokes, so the wheat seems to sway in the wind.
Q476458: Find the three swords in the father's hand and the three brothers' arms reaching for them. Now count the arches in the background — there are three too!
It is a story from Ancient Rome: three brothers promise to defend their city. Jacques-Louis David painted it clear and simple, like a stage, and his style became the new fashion.
Q549847: Find little Cupid at the top with a blindfold over his eyes — he is aiming his bow. Then look at the goddess Flora's dress: it is covered in flowers!
Sandro Botticelli painted the magical garden of the goddess Venus. Plant experts have counted about 190 different flowers in it, and many are easy to recognise.
Q523974: See how the shadow of the clouds covers part of the town, while the roofs far away shine in the sun. Find the tiny people on the shore.
Johannes Vermeer made the sparkles on boats and roofs with tiny dots of light paint. The writer Marcel Proust called it the most beautiful painting in the world.
Q1025704: Find the stars in the dark blue sky — they look like flowers. See how the yellow lamplight falls on the tables and the cobblestones.
Vincent van Gogh painted this night scene right there in the street. He was proud to paint a night picture without using any black at all.
Q1267893: Find the spiky juniper bush behind her. In Italian, 'juniper' sounds almost like her name — Ginevra!
It is the only painting by Leonardo da Vinci in the Americas. His fingerprints were found in the paint: he softened it with his fingers.
Q500985: Find the hunters and their dogs coming home. Then look down at the frozen ponds for tiny people skating!
Pieter Brueghel the Elder painted a whole series about the seasons, and this one is winter. He places us up on a hill, looking down over the whole valley.
Q734834: In the middle, find the lamb on the altar, with people coming from every side. Look at its eyes — they look surprisingly human!
Hubert van Eyck began this huge folding altarpiece and his brother Jan finished it. When it was cleaned recently, the lamb turned out to have an almost human face, and the whole world was amazed.
Q563727: Find little Jesus hugging a lamb. Look how blue and misty the mountains are far away!
Leonardo da Vinci noticed that faraway things look bluish and blurry, so he painted the mountains that way. He worked on it for many years and never quite finished it.
Q604761: See how the blue satin suit shines like real fabric. Find the hat in the boy's hand.
Scientists used X-rays and found a dog hidden under the paint: Thomas Gainsborough had painted over it. The boy's costume is old-fashioned, like clothes from a hundred years earlier.
Q1245354: Find the acrobat's legs in little green shoes in the top left corner! On the counter, look for the bowl of oranges and the bottles.
Behind the barmaid hangs a big mirror, but its reflection looks 'wrong' and is shifted to one side. Édouard Manet puzzled us on purpose, and people still argue about it.
Q1142058: Find the flower Mary is giving the baby. See how seriously he studies it — like a little scientist!
Young Leonardo da Vinci painted Mary as a cheerful young mum, smiling and playing with her son. It is named after the Benois family, who sold it to the Hermitage Museum.
Q533619: Find the man banging his head against a wall and the one throwing roses to pigs. What other silly things can you spot?
Pieter Brueghel the Elder hid more than a hundred sayings here and showed each one literally. 'Throwing roses to pigs' means giving something good to someone who won't value it.
Q1133420: Count the long lances on the right — there are so many that the painting got the nickname 'The Lances'. Find the big horse turned away from us.
The winner does not let the defeated commander kneel, but puts a friendly hand on his shoulder. Diego Velázquez showed that kindness is possible even in war.
Q328079: Find the two little angels at the bottom, leaning on their elbows and gazing up dreamily. Now look closely at the clouds — they are made of lots of tiny angel faces!
Those two angels became more famous than the whole painting and appear on postcards, mugs and stamps. Raphael drew back green curtains, like in a theatre, so Mary seems to step towards us.
Q674846: Find the clock on the wall — it is already past midnight! See the bright rings of light glowing around the lamps.
Vincent van Gogh used red and green to show the restless mood of a café at night. He painted it over three nights and slept during the day.
Q1231009: Look: Napoleon is placing the crown not on himself but on his wife, Josephine. Find Napoleon's mother sitting in a box in the middle.
In real life Napoleon's mother was not there, but he asked the painter to add her. The painting is huge — almost ten metres wide!
Q1464531: Find the couple strolling by the river at the bottom. In the sky, look for the seven stars of the Plough — they make the shape of a saucepan.
Vincent van Gogh painted it at night, right on the riverbank. The yellow gas lamps shine in the water as long, wobbly stripes.
Q1070896: Find the people holding on to a piece of the broken mast. See how the warm sun breaks through the storm — a sign of hope!
Sailors believed that the ninth wave in a storm is the biggest. Ivan Aivazovsky painted the sea from memory in his studio, and he could make waves look see-through.
Q1170315: Look closely: the square is not perfectly even, and thin cracks run across the black paint. Other colours peep through them!
Kazimir Malevich wanted to show that a painting can be just a shape and a feeling, not a picture of something. At its first show he hung it high in a corner, where Russian homes kept icons.
Q2200610: Find the house with green shutters — this is where the artist lived. In the distance, look for a train crossing a bridge with puffs of steam.
Vincent van Gogh rented this yellow house in Arles and dreamed it would be a home for artists. His friend, the painter Paul Gauguin, came to stay with him.
Q1213917: Find where the path splits in two in front of the church, and the woman walking along it. What colour is the daytime sky here?
Vincent van Gogh gave the church wavy walls, as if it were alive and moving. He made the sky deep blue, even though it is daytime.
Q1926628: Find the big yellow sun and its shining reflection on the right. Count the people picking grapes among the red leaves.
It is one of the very few paintings Vincent van Gogh sold in his lifetime. It was bought by a painter named Anna Boch.
Q175628: Count the barge haulers — how many are pulling the rope? In the middle, find the young man in a pink shirt lifting his head and fixing his strap.
Barge haulers pulled boats along the river with ropes — very hard work. Ilya Repin travelled to the Volga and drew real haulers from life.
Q1044742: Find the monkey on a lead next to the lady with the parasol! Then look closer: the whole picture is made of tiny coloured dots.
Georges Seurat placed dots of pure colour side by side, and our eyes mix them from far away. He worked on this big painting for about two years.
Q783215: See where John is pointing his finger — up to the sky. Find the thin cross made of reed in his other hand.
Light falls on John out of the darkness, and his mysterious smile is like the Mona Lisa's. Leonardo da Vinci kept this painting with him until the end of his life.
Q930137: Find the lightning in the sky above the town. Then look for a white stork on one of the roofs!
Nobody knows what story this painting tells — it is a mystery. Under the paint, scientists found another figure: Giorgione changed his mind and painted the young man there instead.
Q354396: Find the patterns on the golden dress that look like eyes. How many 'eyes' can you count?
Gustav Klimt decorated the portrait with real gold and silver, so people call it 'The Woman in Gold'. For many years it was kept from Adele's family, until her niece managed to get it back.
Q656434: Find the thin ribbon across the lady's forehead with a little jewel in the middle. Look at her cheek: there is a reddish glow from her dress.
Nobody knows for sure who the lady is: the painting got its name later, by mistake. But since then, that kind of forehead jewel has been called a 'ferronnière'.
Q2629559: Find the pink shoe flying through the air! On the left, look for the statue of Cupid with his finger to his lips: 'Shh!'
Jean-Honoré Fragonard painted a playful, joking scene in soft pinks and greens. A young man hides in the bushes, while an older man pushes the swing from behind.
Q1212937: Find the lute with a broken string and the two globes on the shelves. At the bottom, look at the strange stretched-out shape — what could it be?
It is a trick picture: stand to the side of the painting and the shape turns into a skull. Hans Holbein the Younger used it to remind people that life is short and precious.
Q1638622: Find the rearing horses in the distance and the big tree in the middle. Can you see that the picture is almost all brown and yellow, with no bright colours?
Leonardo da Vinci never finished it because he moved to another city, Milan. So we can see how he started: first the drawing and shadows, colour later.
Q766782: Look at the hands: the man rests his hand gently near her heart, and she lightly touches it. See his golden sleeve — the paint is so thick it stands up like a relief.
Rembrandt laid the paint on thickly, even with a knife, to make the sleeve glow. Vincent van Gogh said he would give ten years of his life to sit in front of it for two weeks.
Q890678: Read it from right to left: a baby on the right, grown-ups in the middle, an old woman on the left. Find the blue statue and the white bird near the old woman.
Paul Gauguin painted this huge picture in Tahiti and asked life's biggest questions in its title. He wrote the title right on the canvas, in the top left corner.
Q969377: Follow the beam of light from the right: it travels with Jesus's pointing hand towards the men at the table. Who is Jesus pointing at?
Caravaggio lit the scene like a spotlight, leaving everything else in the dark. Jesus's hand looks like Adam's hand in Michelangelo's famous ceiling painting.
Q1065493: Find the flowers floating on the water: red poppies, daisies and violets. On the willow branch, look for a little robin.
It is a sad scene from a play by Shakespeare about a girl called Ophelia. John Everett Millais painted the riverbank outdoors for months, and his model posed lying in a bath of warm water.
Q544315: Find the globe covered in stars and constellations that the scientist is touching. Where is the light coming into the room from?
Johannes Vermeer usually painted women, but here he shows a scientist at work. It has a partner painting, 'The Geographer', which seems to show the same man.
Q588695: Find the painter seen from behind in his striped shirt, and the girl holding a trumpet and a book. On the wall, look at the big map with folds in it.
Johannes Vermeer loved this painting so much that he never sold it. After he died, his family tried hard to keep it too.
Q546241: See how Mary and the baby press their cheeks together. Find the little hand he puts around his mother's neck.
An unknown painter in Constantinople made this icon almost nine hundred years ago. It was repainted many times, but the faces of Mary and the baby are still the original ones.
Q185255: Find the musicians right in the middle: the story goes that the painter put himself and his artist friends among them. How many guests can you count?
It is the biggest painting in the Louvre, and it hangs right opposite the Mona Lisa. Paolo Veronese painted more than a hundred people in it.
Q500951: Find the yellow fields and the orange-red trees. Count the women in white caps sitting at the bottom, and find a man climbing over a wall.
Paul Gauguin based it on a wooden carving from a chapel in Brittany and made it bright yellow, like autumn fields. He used flat, bold colours with dark outlines, like stained glass.
Q2246489: Count the people in the boat. Find the one looking straight at us — people say it is Rembrandt himself!
It is Rembrandt's only painting of the sea. It was stolen from a museum in Boston in 1990 and is still missing; an empty frame hangs in its place.
Q3869871: Find the white flower behind the ear of the girl in front. Look at the bright yellow and green fields behind them!
Paul Gauguin painted it in Tahiti, where he went looking for a simple life and bright colours. It was sold as one of the most expensive paintings in the world.
Q687182: Find the dark patterned curtain on the left and the framed picture on the wall. Which colours did the artist use most?
Its real title is 'Arrangement in Grey and Black', because James McNeill Whistler thought about colours like music. His mother was meant to pose standing, but she got tired, so he let her sit.
Q586035: Find the woman sewing in the doorway and the two children playing on the pavement. In the narrow passage, look for another woman at work.
Johannes Vermeer painted a real street in his town, Delft. Not long ago, a researcher used old records to find exactly where this house stood.
Q14866847: Find the yellow sunset sky and the crooked trees with twisty branches. In the distance, look for the ruins of an old abbey on the hill.
For many years this painting lay in an attic, and people thought it was a fake. In 2013 experts proved it is a real Van Gogh: he even described it in a letter to his brother.
Q1217213: Look at the angel's wings: they look like the wings of a real bird. Find the flowers in the grass and the misty mountains far away.
Leonardo da Vinci was only about twenty when he painted it. He copied the wings from real birds, and later another painter made them longer.
Q1473546: The painting is round, like a plate! See how the baby is passed over Mary's shoulder, and find little John behind them.
Michelangelo was a sculptor first, so his people look strong and solid, like statues. It is the only finished panel painting we know for sure he made himself.
Q512755: Look at the father's hands on his son's back: one is big and strong, the other thinner and gentler. Find the son's worn-out shoe — and his other foot is bare.
It tells the story of a son who left home and then came back, and his father forgave him. Rembrandt painted it near the end of his life, and warm light falls on the two of them.
Q2666439: Count the bears: how many cubs are there, and where is their mother? Look at the morning mist between the tall pine trees.
Two artists painted it: Ivan Shishkin did the forest, and Konstantin Savitsky did the bears. Later Savitsky's signature was removed, so for a long time people credited Shishkin alone.
Q1327676: Find the little bird, a goldfinch, in the baby's hand. Look through the two windows: there are blue mountains outside.
Mary looks tenderly at her son as she feeds him — it is a painting about a mother's love. Experts argue whether Leonardo da Vinci painted it himself or a pupil helped him.
Q698015: Find the red carnation in Mary's hand — the baby is reaching for it. Nearby, look for a glass vase full of flowers.
Young Leonardo da Vinci loved nature and carefully painted the see-through vase and the flowers. Through the windows he showed sharp, rocky mountains, like in a fairy tale.
Q920030: Find the painter himself in the shadows on the left, beside a big canvas. Count all the members of the royal family — how many are there?
Francisco Goya borrowed the idea from Velázquez, who also painted himself next to a royal family. One lady is turning away: the prince's bride had not been chosen yet, so nobody knew her face.
Q984058: Find the spinning wheel on the left: it is turning so fast that you can hardly see its spokes! At the back, in the bright room, look at the big tapestry.
Hidden here is the old myth of Arachne, who challenged the goddess Athena to see who could weave better. Diego Velázquez painted the wheel blurry to show how fast it spins.
Q1059211: Find the two angels on the left holding the robes. The one nearest the edge was painted by young Leonardo da Vinci!
It is a painting by his teacher, Andrea del Verrocchio, and his pupils helped in the workshop. Legend says the teacher saw Leonardo's angel and decided to give up painting.
Q1167178: In the middle, find the painter at his easel and the little boy watching him paint. On the floor, look for a white cat!
Gustave Courbet painted himself in his studio, surrounded by friends and all kinds of people of his time. When a big exhibition turned it down, he built his own pavilion to show it.
Q1167907: Find the young woman in a flowery hat playing with a little dog. At the top, look at the striped awning.
Pierre-Auguste Renoir asked his friends to pose on a summer terrace by the river. The girl with the dog is Aline, who later became his wife.
Q1192570: Count the men walking in a line, holding each other's sticks and shoulders. Find the one who has already tumbled into the ditch, and look at the church in the distance.
Pieter Brueghel the Elder painted an old saying: if the blind lead the blind, both fall into a ditch. It means we should choose wise guides.
Q471289: Find the little bunch of white snowdrops in the angel's hand. Look at the boy in black: he is staring straight at us.
Two boys gently carry an angel with a bandage over its eyes, and nobody knows what happened. Hugo Simberg never explained it, and Finnish people voted it their favourite national painting.
Q2366825: Find the dog on the riverbank and the little cottage on the left. See how the horses pull the cart right through the water!
John Constable painted the English countryside where he grew up. His little white dots of light on leaves and water sparkled so much that people called them 'Constable's snow'.
Q1239950: Look at the tables: you can't see their legs, so they seem to float in a zigzag. Where is the man with the pipe looking, and where is the woman looking?
Edgar Degas asked two friends, an actress and an artist, to pose in a real café in Paris. He showed that people can sit side by side and still feel lonely.
Q318947: Find the fruit basket on the very edge of the table — it looks ready to fall out towards us! Look at the arms reaching right out of the picture too.
Caravaggio wanted us to feel we are sitting at this table, as if it is all happening next to us. It is also unusual that Jesus is shown young, without a beard.
Q2546309: Find the hand touching the soft fur collar — see how every single hair is painted. Look for the writing and the 'AD' monogram on both sides.
Albrecht Dürer painted himself facing straight towards us, which was usually done only in holy pictures. In the writing he tells us he painted himself at the age of 28.
Q2629423: Find the big cushion behind the girl's back. Now look at her collar: can you see quick little scratches in the paint?
Fragonard painted very fast and scratched the collar with the end of his brush. Scientists found another face hidden underneath: at first she was looking at us!
Q603751: Find the bride: she sits in front of a green cloth, under a paper crown. Then find the little child in a big hat eating from a plate on the floor.
Look how the pies are carried: on an old door taken off its hinges! Brueghel loved to paint village people having fun.
Q500554: Look at the old man's hands covering his face. Can you find the little fire glowing in the fireplace?
The man is very sad, and van Gogh wanted us to feel kindness for him. He made this painting from his own drawing of years before.
Q2344505: Find the little bird in the boys' hands — it is a goldfinch. Which boy is gently stroking it?
Long ago the house where it hung fell down, and the painting broke into many pieces. People glued them together, and restorers made it shine again.
Q1651874: Look at the children's faces glowing in the dark. Where does the light come from? It is hidden behind a boy!
The machine in the middle shows how the planets move around the Sun. The hidden lamp plays the Sun, so the faces glow like little moons.
Q2293936: Look at the young man's lips and skin: are they rosy, or a little greenish? Find the grapes in his hands and the peaches on the table.
Caravaggio painted himself with the help of a mirror when he was ill. That is why the god of grapes and feasts looks so pale.
Q2735507: Look at the lady's shiny white dress and pink sash. Is she lying on a sofa full of soft cushions?
Goya painted the same lady, in the same pose, twice. The two paintings hang side by side in the Prado museum.
Q2030685: Find the young man breaking a stick over his knee. Now look at the temple at the top: it has many sides, like a crystal.
In the story, only Joseph's stick burst into flowers, so he married Mary. Raphael proudly wrote his name on the temple.
Q334360: Find the broken church wall among the bare, crooked oak trees. Can you spot the tiny figures walking slowly through the gate?
Friedrich painted it as a pair with another picture, ‘The Monk by the Sea’. Its misty, quiet colours make us feel the stillness of winter.
Q474024: Look at Cupid's cheeky smile and his dark wings. Count the things on the floor: a violin, a lute, armour, sheets of music…
Its name means ‘Love conquers all’. The playful god of love steps over music, science and even armour.
Q2338404: Look at the young man's hand: he holds a sheet of paper with music notes. Look at his bright, shining eyes.
It is thought to be Leonardo da Vinci's only portrait of a man. Some parts, like his clothes, were never finished.
Q877191: Find three men: one young, one grown-up and one old. What is the young man looking at? Find the dark cave on the left.
Nobody knows for sure who these three men are. Some think they are wise men studying the sky and the stars.
Q883994: Look at the stormy sky: what colours can you find in it? Find the bridge and the tall towers on the green hill.
El Greco painted his city under a dramatic storm. He even moved some buildings around so the picture would look better.
Q1195035: Look at the lady's shiny silk dress: how many folds can you count? Look at the man's foot on the step: is he about to leave?
It became the most famous kiss in Italian painting. Many people saw in it Italy's hope to become a free, united country.
Q2521909: Find the painter himself in the crowd: he carries a box of paints and brushes on his head. Look at the bright lightning in the sky.
Bryullov visited the ruins of Pompeii and worked on this huge picture for years. He showed people helping and protecting each other when the volcano woke up.
Q1217003: Look at the lady's velvet hat with a white feather. She sits in an open carriage: what does the wintry city behind her look like?
Nobody knows who this lady was, because Kramskoi never told anyone. That is why the picture is called ‘Unknown Woman’.
Q568847: Look at the top corners: tiny crossbows are painted there. Find two people bending in the same curved shape — Mary and Jesus.
The figures look like painted statues standing in a golden box. Rogier painted their tears so carefully that they look real and shiny.
Q597114: Look up at the big red curtain. Find the people around Mary: how do they show that they are sad?
The church that ordered it said no, because Mary looked like a simple, ordinary woman. But artists loved it, and Rubens helped a duke to buy it.
Q194137: Look at the sharp slabs of ice piled up like a tower. Can you find the ship trapped in the ice on the right?
Friedrich studied real ice on a frozen river near his home. Nobody wanted to buy this picture while he was alive, but now it is very famous.
Q700251: Find the big picture of Cupid on the wall behind the girl. Can you see her face reflected in the window glass?
For hundreds of years Cupid was hidden under paint added after Vermeer's time. Restorers carefully removed it, and Cupid appeared again!
Q969367: Look closely at the scales in her hand: is there anything in the little pans? Find the pearls and gold on the table.
The scales are empty: she is just checking that they balance. Soft light from the window makes everything feel calm and quiet.
Q775407: Look at the bright green railing and shutters. Peek into the dark room behind: can you see a boy in the shadows?
The lady sitting on the left is Berthe Morisot, who was a painter too. Manet's friends seem to be thinking about different things, each in their own world.
Q1219263: Find the lion sniffing the sleeping woman. What lies next to her? Look for the mandolin and the water jug.
The lion does not hurt her: everything is calm under the moon, like in a dream. Rousseau taught himself to paint and never saw a real desert.
Q1899740: Find the bright red colours: on Mary's dress and on the people below. Look at the crowd of little angels carrying her up.
It is huge, almost seven metres tall, and stands above the altar of a church in Venice. Titian made it so bright that you can see it from the church door.
Q794077: Find little Cupid between the two ladies, playing with the water. Look far behind: find the castle on one side and the church tower on the other.
The two ladies look almost like twins, but one is dressed up and the other is not. People still argue about what Titian meant — it is a beautiful riddle.
Q1167796: Find the white bird inside the big glass bowl. Can you spot the moon peeking through the window?
A scientist shows how a pump takes the air out of the glass. Nobody knows if he will let the air back in, so the girls worry about the bird.
Q2011510: Look at the bowl of fruit: can you find a bruised apple and leaves with holes? Look at the glass jug of wine on the table.
Experts found a tiny picture of Caravaggio hidden in the reflection on the wine jug! He painted himself at work by his easel.
Q2610675: Watch the girl's fingers closely: while she reads his palm, she is secretly slipping off his ring!
Caravaggio painted ordinary people from the street instead of saints and kings. The young man is so busy looking at her that he does not notice the trick.
Q1368055: Find the three women bending down to pick up grain. Now look far behind them: find the huge haystacks and a man on a horse.
After the harvest, poor people were allowed to pick up the leftover ears of wheat. Millet showed these hard-working women as strong and important.
Q405814: Find the people trying to bite a hanging pancake without using their hands. Can you spot the roast chicken tied to the mast?
Bosch made a funny picture about silly people who forgot where their boat was going. Look: the mast is a real tree with leaves!
Q2664039: Look at the lady's black dress and her very pale skin. Find the thin golden straps on her shoulders.
At first Sargent painted one strap slipping off her shoulder, and people were shocked. He repainted it and called the picture ‘Madame X’ instead of using her name.
Q2339059: Find the dark train rushing towards you over the bridge. Can you spot a tiny hare running in front of it?
Trains were new and exciting in Turner's time. He painted rain, steam and speed with soft, blurry swirls of colour.
Q1167932: Look at the glowing hand writing letters on the wall. Find the wine spilling from the golden cups.
In this Bible story, a mysterious hand writes a warning to a proud king. Rembrandt wrote the Hebrew letters in columns, from top to bottom.
Q1516449: Look between the pillars: find a river, a bridge and a whole tiny town. Can you spot two little people peeking over the wall, and the peacocks in the garden?
Van Eyck painted the tiniest things so carefully that you almost need a magnifying glass. Look how many little people are crossing the bridge!
Q210277: Find Manet himself: he stands at the very left edge. Look for the children playing at the front with their toys.
Manet painted his friends at an outdoor concert in a Paris park. He used quick, loose brushstrokes, and many people thought it looked unfinished.
Q45130: Find the globe on top of the cupboard. What is the man holding in his hand? It is a tool for measuring maps.
The geographer has stopped working to think and gazes out of the window. Vermeer painted him as a pair with another picture, ‘The Astronomer’.
Q1652023: Find the bright glowing light inside the glass flask. Who is kneeling in front of it? Can you spot the moon in the window?
An alchemist was hunting for gold and found phosphorus, a stuff that glows in the dark! Wright of Derby loved painting bright lights in dark rooms.
Q488825: Find the man in the yellow cloak on the right, looking straight at us. That is Botticelli himself!
Botticelli painted members of the rich Medici family as the three wise kings. It is like a family photo hidden inside a Bible story.
Q2627056: Look at David's face. Does he look happy that he won, or a little sad and thoughtful?
This is the Bible story of young David, who beat the giant Goliath. Caravaggio gave the defeated giant his own face.
Q2409245: Look at her eyes: she glances at us from the corner, a little shy. Find her tall black hat and her necklace.
It is one of the first portraits set in a real room, not against a flat dark wall. That makes it feel as if she is really here.
Q166937: Find the big map on the wall behind her. Look at her blue jacket: how many shades of blue can you find?
Vermeer used a very expensive blue paint made from a precious stone. There is no window in the picture, but soft light falls on her from the left.
Q432253: Count the flags flapping in the wind. How many boats can you find on the sea?
The man sitting in the chair is Monet's father. Monet painted the picture in three bright stripes: garden, sea and sky.
Q948034: Look at the lady's big puffy sleeve: see how many shiny folds Raphael painted! Find the thin veil over her hair.
Many people think she was someone Raphael loved very much. He painted the cloth so softly that you want to touch it.
Q1169395: Find the three musicians: who is playing and who is singing? Look at the black-and-white tiles on the floor.
In 1990 thieves stole this painting from a museum in Boston, and it is still missing. The museum keeps its empty frame on the wall, waiting for it to come home.
Q2336984: Look in the mirror above the instrument: it shows the girl's face, and even part of the painter's easel!
The girl stands with her back to us, but the mirror shows her face. It is a clever trick: Vermeer hid his own studio inside the picture.
Q2360329: Find the golden balls the three girls are holding. Look at the soft green landscape and hills behind them.
This picture is tiny, only a little bigger than a grown-up's hand. Raphael painted it when he was a young man of about twenty.
Q2395218: Can you feel the wind? See how it blows the lady's veil and dress. Find the little boy standing in the grass.
This is Monet's wife Camille and their son Jean. Monet painted fast, outdoors, to catch this sunny, breezy moment before it passed.
Q2983399: Look at all the rushing horses: how many can you count? Find the riders in bright red trousers.
Goya painted the day when the people of Madrid stood up for their city. He wanted everyone to remember how brave ordinary people were.
Q5930190: Find a thin moon on one side and a bright star on the other. Can you spot the two men walking along the road?
Van Gogh painted it in the south of France, where he loved the tall cypress trees. The cypress looks like a dark green flame reaching for the sky.
Q254923: This painting is round, like a plate! Find the little cross that the children are holding.
It is named after the Alba family in Spain, who once owned it. It also once hung in the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg.
Q1171740: Find the bright star in the sky with a ring of light around it. How many windows are glowing?
Astronomers think the bright star is the planet Venus. Using it, they even worked out the exact day van Gogh painted it!
Q663133: Find the cards hidden behind the cheater's back. Look at the older man's glove: the fingertips have holes!
Two tricksters are cheating a young boy at cards. The older one peeks at the boy's cards and secretly signals with his fingers.
Q776175: Find the man sleeping under the tree. What are the others eating for their lunch?
Brueghel painted a set of pictures about the times of the year; this one is late summer. You can almost feel the hot sun on the golden wheat.
Q972196: Find the lion lying at the saint's feet. Look carefully: many parts are only drawn, not coloured in.
Leonardo da Vinci never finished this picture. Long ago it was cut into pieces, but later the pieces were found and joined together again.
Q1118456: Find the bright spots of sunlight on the girl's dress and on the ground. They are little dabs of white and yellow paint.
Renoir wanted to show sunshine falling through the leaves. At first some people laughed and said the spots looked like stains!
Q509806: Find the chunks of ice floating in the river. Can you see the flag fluttering in the cold wind?
It shows a famous night in American history, when soldiers crossed an icy river. Leutze painted it in Germany, and it is enormous: more than six metres long!
Q13528770: Look behind the man: the wall is covered with Japanese pictures! Find a snowy mountain and a lady in a kimono.
Père Tanguy sold paints and was kind to poor artists like van Gogh. Van Gogh loved Japanese prints and filled the background with them.
Q26220165: Find the old church tower behind the trees. Can you see the woman walking in the garden?
Van Gogh painted the garden of his father's house; his father was the village pastor. In 2020 thieves stole it from a museum, but it was found three years later!
Q2610936: Look at the basket: find the grapes, the peaches and a leaf with brown spots. Which fruit would you pick?
The fruit looks so real that you might want to take a bite! Caravaggio painted it when he was young and had just come to Rome.
Q2653851: Find the dog in the bottom corner. Look at the strong men pulling and pushing together, with all their might.
Rubens painted it on three panels that open like doors, for a big church in Antwerp. Everything is moving, as if the picture could come alive.
Q2344437: Look at the top: Jesus floats in bright light. Now look down: how many people are pointing?
It was Raphael's very last painting. People loved it so much that it was placed beside him when everyone came to say goodbye.
Q2439462: Look at her see-through veil: can you see her forehead through it? Find her fingers folded together at the bottom.
Rogier painted the thin veil so well that it looks like real, light cloth. Her calm, lowered eyes make the picture feel very quiet.
Q467376: Find the big map on the wall. Look at the officer's huge hat: why does he look so much bigger than the girl?
He is closer to us, so he looks bigger, like someone standing right next to a camera. Sunlight from the window falls on the laughing girl's face.
Q846213: Look at the girl's glowing orange dress, as thin as a flame. Find the branch with pink flowers in the top corner.
Once nobody wanted to buy this picture, not even for a tiny price. Now it is one of the most famous pictures of a sleeping girl.
Q867403: Look at Mary's very long neck, like a swan's. Find the tiny man next to the tall column at the bottom right.
Parmigianino made everything longer on purpose, to look extra graceful. He never finished it: there were meant to be more columns.
Q1216387: Find the red and white threads spilling out of the sewing cushion. Do they look sharp, or soft and blurry?
It is one of Vermeer's smallest paintings, smaller than a sheet of paper. He painted the near threads blurry, like a camera focused on something else.
Q2035209: Look at the dark background: which colours shine out of it? Find baby Jesus's little hand resting on Mary's dress.
A Grand Duke of Tuscany loved this picture so much that he took it with him everywhere he travelled. That is how it got its name.
Q8030760: Find the colourful parrot sitting on the lady's raised hand. Look at her long hair spread out like a dark fan.
Courbet liked to paint people as they really are, not perfect like statues. The bright parrot is the most colourful thing in the picture.
Q63692: Find the young man on the left, smiling and looking straight at us. Many people think he is Vermeer himself!
It is one of Vermeer's early paintings, and one of only three where he wrote the year. Here he uses bright, warm colours: red, yellow and black.
Q2535473: Look at the three people around the table: who is smiling? Then look at the wall behind them: what is hanging there?
Velázquez painted it when he was only about eighteen. He liked painting simple meals and everyday people, very close up and very real.
Q2734892: Find the patches of sunlight and the cool blue shadows on the white dresses. How many women can you count?
Monet painted this big picture outdoors and even dug a trench to lower the canvas and reach the top. Camille, who later became his wife, posed for almost all the women.
Q3808227: Look at the two girls: one plays, and the other leans over to follow the music. Find the vase of flowers and the curtain.
Renoir painted this scene several times until he was happy with it. The French government bought this version for a museum in Paris.
Q680128: Look at all the faces squeezed together: some are grumpy, some look silly. Find the calm faces of Jesus and of a woman holding a cloth.
Bosch filled the whole picture with faces, like a crowd in a tight squeeze. He made the unkind people look odd, so we notice the kind, calm ones.
Q257580: Find the small dark tugboat with a tall chimney pulling the pale old ship. Look at the fiery sunset on the right.
The old sailing ship once fought in a famous sea battle and is going on its last journey. Turner called it his ‘darling’, and Britain voted it its favourite painting.
Q386453: Find the shiny silver jug and bowl on the table. Where is the light coming from?
Vermeer painted soft window light gliding over the white headscarf and the wall. Everything feels calm, as if time has stopped.
Q951105: Find the dog at the front, near the middle. How many people can you count at this enormous feast?
At first it was called ‘The Last Supper’. Church officials said it had too many funny details, so Veronese simply changed its name!
Q555821: Look at the young man's dark cap and long hair. Where are his eyes looking?
Raphael painted himself when he was very young, in his early twenties. Today this gentle face is one of the best-known faces of any painter.
Q2337873: Look at the angel's fingers: he seems to be counting on them. Look at Matthew's stool: one leg sticks out over the edge, towards you!
The angel is helping Matthew write his book, explaining things one by one. Caravaggio's first version was turned down, so he painted this new one.
Q552040: Find the young knight asleep under a tree. What is each lady holding? One has a book and a sword, the other has flowers.
The knight is dreaming about two ways of life: hard work and learning, or fun and pleasure. The picture is tiny, about the size of a small book.
Q927449: Find the basket of bread that Martha is bringing. Look at Mary sitting at Jesus's feet, listening carefully.
This is Vermeer's biggest painting, made when he was young. Later he painted much smaller, quieter pictures of rooms with windows.
Q930535: Find the pink dress and the red cloth with white flowers. Look at the green sea behind the women, with waves like stripes.
Gauguin sailed to Tahiti, an island far away in the Pacific Ocean. He painted with big flat patches of bright colour, a little like a poster.
